## Abstract

A single ENA study accession, PRJEB1234, was resolved to determine its contents. The query used the BRC/ENA study endpoint, which returns the study record plus its run-level file report. PRJEB1234 is "A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome," secondary study accession ERP002070, first made public 2013-06-06. The study contains 916 sequencing runs. Every run record inspected shares the same library configuration: library strategy WGS, library source GENOMIC, library selection RANDOM, library layout PAIRED, platform ILLUMINA, instrument model Illumina Genome Analyzer, first-public date 2013-06-06, and last-updated date 2018-11-16. Two organisms appear across the runs: *Setaria italica* (NCBI taxon 4555, sample titles of the form "Worldwide foxtail millet accession CiNNN") and *Setaria viridis* (taxon 4556, "Worldwide green foxtail accession CiNNN"). Run depth varies by more than an order of magnitude: the smallest run observed reports 269,167 read pairs / 51,141,730 bases, the largest 6,757,304 reads / 1,283,887,760 bases. Each run carries two gzipped FASTQ files with direct HTTPS download paths. The result matters because it identifies PRJEB1234 as a population-resequencing panel of roughly 900 domesticated and wild *Setaria* accessions at low-to-moderate per-accession coverage, rather than a single-genome project, which determines what analyses the data can support.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** Foxtail millet (*Setaria italica*) is a domesticated C4 panicoid cereal; *Setaria viridis* (green foxtail) is its wild progenitor and a model system for C4 grasses. A "haplotype map" study resequences many accessions at modest depth to catalogue segregating variation rather than to assemble one genome. Knowing which of these two designs an accession represents governs whether the data are usable for variant calling across a panel, for GWAS, or for assembly.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. The ENA study record carries no linked PubMed identifier in the fields returned.

**Knowledge Gap.** The accession PRJEB1234 alone conveys nothing about organism, assay, scale, or data availability.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: resolve PRJEB1234 to its title, organism content, run count, library design, and file availability. No statistical hypothesis applies; this is a record-retrieval task.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** A single accession lookup was required. The BRC-routed ENA study tool was selected because it accepts an ENA project accession directly and returns both study metadata and the per-run file report, including working download URLs. No other resource was queried, since the question was fully answerable from the ENA record.

**Materials.** European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) portal file-report API, reached via `brc_ena_study`. Provenance reported by the tool: `https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport`, parameter `accession=PRJEB1234`.

**Procedures.**
1. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJEB1234")` — no other filters applied.

**Statistical Analysis.** The run total (916) is the `run_count` field returned by the tool, not a count of rows I tabulated. Library-design values (strategy, source, selection, layout, platform, instrument) were read from the `library_strategy`, `library_source`, `library_selection`, `library_layout`, `instrument_platform`, and `instrument_model` fields of the returned run records; they were identical in every record inspected. Organism identity was read from the `tax_id` and `scientific_name` fields. Minimum and maximum read and base counts are the extreme values of the `read_count` and `base_count` fields among the returned records; they are not guaranteed to be the extremes of all 916 runs, because the tool did not state whether the returned record list is complete or paged. No percentages were computed, and no per-species run split is reported, because a reliable denominator for the full 916 was not established.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

Table 1. Study-level record for PRJEB1234.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Study accession | PRJEB1234 |
| Secondary study accession | ERP002070 |
| Study title | A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome |
| First public | 2013-06-06 |
| Project-level tax_id | (empty in record) |
| Run count | 916 |
| Organisms in runs | *Setaria italica*, *Setaria viridis* |

Table 2. Library configuration, identical across all inspected run records.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| library_strategy | WGS |
| library_source | GENOMIC |
| library_selection | RANDOM |
| library_layout | PAIRED |
| instrument_platform | ILLUMINA |
| instrument_model | Illumina Genome Analyzer |
| last_updated | 2018-11-16 |
| FASTQ files per run | 2 |

Table 3. Range of run depth among inspected records.

| Run | Sample title | tax_id | Reads | Bases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ERR215192 | Worldwide foxtail millet accession Ci440 | 4555 | 269,167 | 51,141,730 |
| ERR215080 | Worldwide foxtail millet accession Ci324 | 4555 | 346,817 | 65,895,230 |
| ERR214765 | Worldwide foxtail millet accession Ci003 | 4555 | 1,917,724 | 279,987,704 |
| ERR215678 | Worldwide foxtail millet accession Ci942 | 4555 | 6,158,397 | 1,170,095,430 |
| ERR214976 | Worldwide foxtail millet accession Ci218 | 4555 | 6,757,304 | 1,283,887,760 |

Table 4. Example *Setaria viridis* runs (taxon 4556) within the study.

| Run | Sample title | Sample accession | Reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERR215618 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci879 | SAMEA1906112 | 3,499,448 |
| ERR215556 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci816 | SAMEA1905464 | 697,127 |
| ERR215637 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci900 | SAMEA1905857 | 893,955 |
| ERR215545 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci801 | SAMEA1905903 | 2,517,285 |
| ERR215546 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci802 | SAMEA1905799 | 1,537,783 |
| ERR215549 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci809 | SAMEA1905822 | 1,176,741 |
| ERR215550 | Worldwide green foxtail accession Ci810 | SAMEA1905840 | 527,895 |

**Findings.** PRJEB1234 holds 916 sequencing runs. Every run is paired-end whole-genome shotgun sequencing of genomic DNA with random selection, generated on the Illumina Genome Analyzer. Runs were first released 2013-06-06 and last updated 2018-11-16. Each run maps to one sample accession (SAMEA prefix) and one experiment accession (ERX prefix), and each run's sample title names a distinct accession identifier in the series Ci001–Ci942. Two taxa are present: 4555 (*Setaria italica*, labelled "foxtail millet") and 4556 (*Setaria viridis*, labelled "green foxtail"). Among the records returned, read counts span 269,167 to 6,757,304 and base counts span 51,141,730 to 1,283,887,760. Every run record supplies two `fastq_https` URLs and paired `fastq_bytes` values.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The record answers the question: PRJEB1234 is a population resequencing panel, not a reference-genome project. The combination of 916 runs, one distinct germplasm accession per sample title, uniform paired-end WGS libraries, and per-run yields in the 0.05–1.3 Gb range is the signature of shallow whole-genome resequencing across a diversity panel, consistent with the stated aim of building a haplotype map. The presence of taxon 4556 alongside 4555 means the panel includes wild green foxtail accessions in addition to the domesticate.

**Context.** The tool itself flagged that the study spans more than one organism and that a project-level organism label is not the organism of every run. That flag is borne out: the study record's `tax_id` field is empty, and organism must be read per run. The `Ci` accession numbering runs to at least Ci942, close to but above the 916 run count, so the panel numbering is not perfectly contiguous with the run list.

**Limitations.** The tool reported `run_count: 916` but did not state whether the returned `results` array contains all 916 runs or a truncated page; consequently the minimum and maximum yields in Table 3 are extremes of the inspected records, not established extremes of the study, and no per-species run counts or percentages are reported. `collection_date` is empty in every run record, so no temporal or geographic sampling information is available from this query. No genome coverage figure can be stated, because the query returned no genome size. No publication is linked in the returned fields, so the study cannot be tied to a paper from this evidence alone. The record also cannot establish sequence quality, contamination, or whether all runs passed the submitters' own filters.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** PRJEB1234 = ERP002070, "A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome": 916 paired-end Illumina Genome Analyzer WGS runs over *Setaria italica* and *Setaria viridis* accessions, public since 2013, with FASTQ files downloadable per run. The next queries worth running are a paged retrieval of all 916 runs to obtain exact per-species counts and the true yield distribution, and a PubMed search for the study title to locate the associated publication, which this query did not supply.

## References

[1] European Nucleotide Archive (ENA), study PRJEB1234 / ERP002070 file report — https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport (parameter: `acc
